DELIVERABLE 1 — ranked loss table. Method: re-swept the FIT population (depth 1/2/3 x chaos 0 x seeds 0-119, n=360, pooled — same as round 3/4) against current model.js (unchanged since round 4), this time keeping rate()'s per-band bands array for the WORST-of-3-widths mark of every row (fitness is worst-width, so the loss has to be read off the mark that decides it, not the mean). Reproduced round4.json exactly: mean=67.00 ceiling=78 p10=58, gap from 100 = 33.00. Per-band mean points lost = weight x (1-credit) / (that row's live weight) x 100, averaged over all 360 rows (0 contributed on rows where the band is unread  14 covered/credit==null  14 per the brief's instruction not to count a dropped band as a loss). Sums to 33.04 across the 11 bands, matching the observed 33.00-point gap almost exactly, which cross-checks the accounting against rate()'s own formula.

Four bands (width-used, repetition, measure, contrast) account for 84.1% of the 33-point gap; the other seven account for 15.9%, and two of them (slivers, depth) are at exactly 0.00  14 fully saturated, confirming and sharpening the readme's existing 'five ranges carry no information here' finding (lanes/gap-share/frame-gap/scale also sit at mean credit >=0.89, essentially solved).

Supporting breakdown for width-used and contrast (the two bands with a clean structural story). width-used mean credit by shape: shell 0.139 (n=9), bands 0.256 (75), gallery 0.304 (36), column 0.322 (30), rail 0.354 (57), split 0.431 (69), deck 0.434 (18), mail 0.443 (24), docs 0.482 (42)  14 every shape is under the 0.70 ideal floor, none saturated. By worst-width: 390 mean credit 0.731 (n=162 rows where 390 was the worst width), 3440 mean credit 0.062 (n=178), 1280 mean credit 0.009 (n=20, thin). So width-used is a WIDE-SCREEN failure specifically: raw content-span ratio across all 360 rows has median 0.333 and p10 0.121 against an ideal floor of 0.70  14 half of all rolls use under a third of the width they were given. contrast mean credit by shape: bands 0.655 (75) vs 0.207-0.353 on the other eight (shell/gallery/docs/column/deck/rail/mail/split)  14 bands is the ONLY SHAPES entry whose tracks ever include feature/hero, so 8 of 9 shapes draw a flat heading hierarchy by construction; no AUTHOR range sizes text at all, so there is no emission to tune here.

DELIVERABLE 1  14 the paragraph. Is the dominant loss fixable by changing what gen.js emits, or only by changing what shapes exist? Both, unevenly. repetition (21.0% of the gap, mean credit 0.012, in the weakest-3 of 98.9% of rolls) and contrast (17.1%, credit 0.2-0.4 on 8 of 9 shapes) are STRUCTURAL: repetition is the direct cost of a part vocabulary built from N identically-classed repeated children (COUNTS on wall/index/main), which is what a card wall or a nav list IS  14 no range moves it without changing which parts exist, matching this readme's existing repetition finding. contrast is flat because only the `bands` shape ever draws a `feature`/`hero` track and no AUTHOR range controls heading size at all  14 there is no emission to widen. width-used, the single largest band (28.1%, mean credit 0.062 whenever 3440 is the worst width vs 0.731 at 390), IS an emission, and it is entangled with measure (17.9%, mean credit 0.600) through the SAME line: gen.js's claim() applies the `flow measure start --measure:Xem` cap (AUTHOR.measure, 27-34em) to any LEAF whose drawn part is sections/notes  14 not just genuine prose-role tracks  14 so 46% of main, 18% of wall and 14% of index leaves collapse to a centred ~30em column inside a row that may be 3440px wide, regardless of how much room the row actually has. That rule is a deliberate, documented fix (readme: 117 chars/line at 1920 without it) so narrowing the fix back is a real trade against measure, not a free win. Net: about 38% of the gap (repetition + contrast) needs new shapes/parts and is out of this task's reach; about 28% (width-used) traces to one named emission  14 the PROSE.test(drawn) branch of claim()'s measure calculation  14 and is what deliverable 3 targets, gated to fire only for the genuine prose role in row-direction (dir!==\"v\") shapes so the column/bands document-style reading columns are untouched. The remaining ~34% (pad-share, lanes, gap-share, frame-gap, scale, slivers, depth) is spread thin across seven bands already averaging credit >=0.75, i.e. near the generator's structural ceiling on those  14 no single knob among them is worth turning.

DELIVERABLE 2 — choices widened. gen.js's roll() now logs every COUNTS/DEPTHS/INNER/ROLES/TONES/AUTHOR draw into new array keys on choices (author, roles, depths, inner, counts, tones), alongside the unchanged five scalar keys (seed, fit, depth, chaos, masthead/shape/foot). Caught and fixed one real bug on the way: my first pass reordered the two RNG draws inside part() (count-then-role instead of role-then-count), which silently reseeded every downstream draw for every seed — mean jumped 67.00→68.47, ceiling 78→79, p10 58→60 on a re-sweep. Restored draw order; re-verified bit-identical: FIT n=360 mean=67.00 ceiling=78 p10=58, HELD n=360 mean=67.26 ceiling=78 p10=57 — exact match to round4.json both pools. credit() and proposal() are byte-identical to round4.json's output for all five original keys (shape, fit, depth, chaos, masthead) — verified by direct JSON comparison, not eyeballed. No weights refit.

log.msg: DELIVERABLE 4 — null result, reverted. Gated claim()'s incidental sections/notes measure-cap to dir==="v" only (one line), re-swept FIT (seeds 0-119) and HELD (seeds 10000-10119), n=360 each, against round4 baseline (FIT mean 66.997 ceiling 78 p10 58; HELD mean 67.261 ceiling 78 p10 57). Result: FIT mean 66.869 (−0.13, −0.30 SE) ceiling 78 (+0) p10 57 (−1); HELD mean 67.042 (−0.22, −0.63 SE) ceiling 78 (+0) p10 57 (+0). Held-out got WORSE, not better, and by more SE than FIT did — not an overfitting signature, a real (if modest) regression: measure's credit loss from the newly-uncapped row-direction leaves cost more than width-used's credit gain paid back. Per the brief, reverted — gen.js's claim() is back to the original PROSE.test(drawn) rule (unconditional on dir), now with a comment recording the tried-and-reverted experiment and its numbers so a future session doesn't re-spend the sweep re-deriving the same idea. Verified byte-identical to round4.json post-revert: FIT 67.00/78/58, HELD 67.26/78/57. The width-used/measure entanglement named in deliverable 1's paragraph is real, but this particular lever nets negative — the fixable third of the gap needs a cleverer edit than a blanket dir gate, or it needs to stay unfixed.
